I am still living under parents’ control. This means that there are many things I cannot decide but the parents have to do so.

Education is the act of gaining knowledge and skills that can help one control his life and live with people in the community.
Going to school is everybody’s right in the community so that he or she can live a good life.
We go to school to get knowledge over the world issues.
[Is it useful to get an education?] All respondents: Yes.
[Why?] Education is a key to life.
Education fights ignorance from people and the community at large.
Education helps to solve different problems in the community.
[How?] For example doctors are able to treat sick people in the community and this is a product of education. Soldiers also protect citizens against their enemies.
All respondents agree that most boys in this community end at Form IV and girls at Form II.
[Why do most boys end at Form IV and girls at Form II?] Girls get pregnant.
Some girls fail to get needs such as food as well as clothes. This makes them stay at home sometimes selling labor so as to get these needs. As time goes by these girls get expelled from school.
All respondents agree that all boys and girls should reach the university level.
[Why?] At the university level everyone is sure that he or she can get employed or start own business.
[Another one?] If one aims at studying to the university level she cannot get pregnancy before attaining her goals.

All respondents agree that parents in this community show more commitment at educating their boys than the girls. The reasons given all concentrate on the point that parents are tired of girls getting pregnant before they can end their studies.

All respondents agree that all men and women participate all together in doing all the agricultural activities.

It is not easy for a young woman who still lives with the parents to grow and then sell crops on their own. However if a young woman lives alone she can grow crops and sell on her own although she would face a problem of getting land on which to do the farming unless she rents land.
[Do we all agree with the speaker?] All respondents: Yes.
The same situation as for the young women applies to the young men. They can grow and sell on their own the time they no longer live with their parents.
[Do we all agree with the speaker?] All respondents: Yes.

[How is it decided who farms which plot?] Most of the households in this community do the farming on the same plots. The land itself is not enough to allow each household member to prepare his or her own plot.

[Are there no household members responsible for some farm plots while other household members are responsible for other plots in this community?] What happens is that different plots are rented from different areas of this village and all household members will go farming or participating in farming activities until all the plots are cleared.
[Do we all agree that there are no households where some household members are in charge of certain plots while others are in charge of other plots?] All respondents: Yes.
There are is no this case whereby women have separate plots while men have their own plots.
All the farming activities are done by all household members until all the plots are cleared.
All respondents: Yes.
If you have money people to work in the farm are available.
[What about the use of tractors?] Tractors are used by very few people but if you want this service you just need to have money.
All respondents: Yes.
[Which responsibilities are these?] Working to other people’s plots so as to earn some money.
Taking care of the sick might be at home or in the hospitals.
[Another one?] Doing other activities such as business or finding the market for oranges so that they cannot perish in the farm.
Only capital is needed to obtain this labor.
They can invite relatives and family members, prepare food and drinks and then have the farming activities done.
This would only be through hiring the human labor to do activities they want done.
All respondents: Yes.
[Whom could they consult?] She could consult her husband or other household members for advice.
[Another one?] She can consult the agricultural extension officers.
She can also consult other people in the village who are famous of having knowledge on a new crop she wants to plant.
All respondents: Yes.
[Whom could he consult?] He can consult the agricultural extension officer too.
He can discuss the matter with his wife or anyone else in the family.

All men and women are equal.
[How?] It means that no one should mistreat the other. A woman should not mistreat the man neither should a man mistreat the woman.
Having fair competition in leadership competition. It means that women are also encouraged to engage in politics.
[Another one?] Gender equality it means that a woman and a man help one another in doing various activities.
[Do you think gender equality is a good or a bad thing?] Gender equality is good if it is used well.
[How?] Some women take the chance of gender equality to mistreat their men by overworking them.
[Another one?] This helps to make women and girls do other activities that men also do. Girls today have football teams and are encouraged to go for militia services.

Once a woman is married she can walk alone to the market but not comfortable as she used to do the time she was not married because whoever person she talks to implies a lot to other people and to the husband in case he came to see her talk to such people.
When the women are married they walk comfortably but keeping time to go back home because they now have more responsibilities than the time when they were not married.
It is hard for them because the market is far from this village. Few women go to sell goods at XX centre for example but the rest do sell small goods such as pancakes in the village.
[Do we all agree with the speaker?] All respondents: Yes.

Out of every 10 women, how many move freely on their own in public spaces (private rating): 1 (practically no women move freely on their own in the village): 0 votes; 2: 0 votes; 3: 1 vote; 4: 1 vote; 5: 0 votes; 6: 0 votes; 7: 0 votes; 8: 1 vote; 9: 6 votes; 10 (practically all women move freely on their own in the village): 1 vote
All respondents come to an agreement that about eight women out of ten can move freely on their own in the public spaces of the community.
[Why do you think are the reasons as to why women are able to move freely in the community?] The men in this community are not very hard to their women as long as they are going to do a right thing.
By all means women have to move if search of water and other needs of which they have to pass in public spaces.

It is very easy for them to move because parents find no reason to prevent them from moving as they are going to work for their needs. However after they get there, most of them face difficult life that force them to return home.
[Is there another person with a different idea?] All respondents: No.
Many people despise these people that they moved to town thinking that they could get good life but they have now returned badly off.
[Do all boys or men that move to town return badly off?] All respondents: No.
Some do win in life and return with money that they use to do better things at home.
[What opportunities do they have after they return?] They come with better clothes whereas some come to help their parents.
Some return when they have changed the ways they used to dress, cut hair or talk. They live more of a town lifestyle.
All respondents get to an agreement that most of the men do marry at the age of 30 years whereas women get married at the age of 21 years.

The decisions are reached after the man and woman wanting to marry one another have agreed to marry one another. They will discuss the matter with parents and relatives and at the end they will get married.
